title: Spotify to Introduce New Paid AI Tool for Remixing Music

summary:
Spotify is developing a new artificial intelligence service that allows subscribers to manipulate the artist or genre of songs on the platform, including simulating one musician covering another's track. The tool is targeted for a launch in the first quarter of 2027 and may cost an additional $4-$5 a month, with an official unveiling scheduled around the Grammys in February.

The feature will be restricted to artists who opt in, and Spotify will pay royalties from the resulting remixes to the original performers. While the company has secured licensing deals with Universal Music, Merlin, Believe, and Kobalt, it remains in negotiations with Sony and Warner.

selectedTweets.text:
BREAKING: Spotify is targeting Q1 2027 for an AI remix service that would let Premium users make one artist appear to cover another’s song or turn a folk track into dance music, the FT reports. It may cost an extra $4–$5 a month, with an unveiling around February’s Grammys.

Artists would opt in. Royalties from fan-made remixes would go to the original artists, and remix streams would count toward the originals on Spotify’s charts. Universal Music, Merlin, Kobalt and Believe have signed deals; Sony Music and Warner Music are still negotiating.
